effective.basis: Old state: UDE official card rulings (Sangan/Witch: 'If you have no eligible monsters, your opponent gets to see your Deck to verify', captured 2005-06-16) through Konami's own per-set rulings documents - Machina Mayhem (2010-04-06, 18 days before the Edison snapshot), Starstrike Blast (2010-11-16), Storm of Ragnarok (2011-02-02). New state: KDE-US Tournament Policy section 'Card/Hand/Deck Verification' forbids verifying the opponent's Deck (first located capture 2019-04-03; still current in v2.5, 2025-09-05). No dated announcement of the change was found, so the interval 2011-02-02 .. 2019-04-03 stays open.

corroboration.title: UDE official Yu-Gi-Oh! Card Rulings (capture 2005-06-16, inside the GOAT window)
corroboration.quote: You must show your opponent the monster you select from your Deck for this card's effect. If you have no eligible monsters, your opponent gets to see your Deck to verify.

corroboration.title: Konami, Machina Mayhem Structure Deck Card Rulings, compiled April 6th 2010 (18 days before the Edison snapshot)
corroboration.quote: If you do not have "Commander Covington" in your Deck, your opponent can ask to verify.

corroboration.title: Konami, Storm of Ragnarok Card Rulings, compiled February 2 2011 - the latest positive attestation of the old state
corroboration.quote: If there is no longer a monster in your hand that you can Special Summon when this effect resolves, your opponent may briefly verify that this is the case.

transitions.historical_text: Discard this card from your hand to the Graveyard to add up to 2 "Thunder Dragon" cards from your Deck to your hand. Then shuffle your Deck. You can only use this effect during your Main Phase.
transitions.summary: Period procedure, not a text erratum: after the discard, if no "Thunder Dragon" remains in the Deck, the goat script proves the whiff by revealing the Deck - the else branch is guarded by 'elseif not Duel.IsExistingMatchingCard(s.thfilter,tp,LOCATION_DECK,0,1,nil) then Duel.GoatConfirm(tp,LOCATION_DECK)', so it fires only on a genuine failed search and not when the player merely declines to add. The modern script never reveals; the printed text is untouched by this.

transitions.historical_text: Discard this card from your hand to the Graveyard to add up to 2 "Thunder Dragon" cards from your Deck to your hand. Then shuffle your Deck. You can only use this effect during your Main Phase.
transitions.summary: Two era allowances the printed text does not show: the goat script can be activated with no copy in the Deck (target check relaxed from Duel.IsExistingMatchingCard to 'return true', with SetOperationInfo count 1 -> 0), and it lets the player add ZERO copies (Duel.SelectMatchingCard minimum 1 -> 0), matching the netrep ruling upstream quotes in its annotation that this card "may be discarded to search for 0" copies. The modern script requires a copy in the Deck to activate and forces at least one to be added. Nothing in the packet dates either allowance, so the chronology is unresolved.

review.notes: Baseline implements lineage v2 (DB2-EN058, exact cdb match); v0/v1 (MRD) precede it with the same behaviour. Trailing v2 -> v5 (LCKC-EN067) is cosmetic: cost/effect rewording ('Discard this card from your hand to the Graveyard to add' -> 'You can discard this card;') and, at v4 (RP01-EN040), the loss of the 'only during your Main Phase' clause. That clause loss is not recorded as functional: the effect registration (type, range, timing) is identical in the goat and modern scripts - the diff touches only the target/operation functions - so upstream implements the same activation window either way. The packet's Retro Pack NA date (2024-08-23) is anomalous against its EU date (2008-07-08); nothing here is dated from that printing. Reveal and the relaxed condition are recorded separately because only the reveal has sourced bounds; the intermediate state needs no implementation, as GOAT (2005-04-01) and Edison (2010-04-24) both precede 2011-02-02.
